analysis:
The PR is docs-only: docs/architecture/inference.md bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds one table row at head line 1387 documenting `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens`. The row says the paged complete store's effective-token floor applies to dense Qwen3.5/3.8, and that a range ends just below the prompt end when that saves at least the floor. It references EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift and the prefix-cache.md streamed-complete-checkpoints section. No code, auth, crypto, or config changed. I also read both head_text units (the GLM, calibration and deadline sections) and found no new behavior there; they are unchanged context.

Threat relevance: T-041 (prefix cache, TTFT oracle, at-rest artifacts) is the only one touched. Per the documentation, the demanded boundary only changes where checkpoints are captured, so more or earlier donations might occur. I saw nothing indicating a change to the HMAC lookup tags, the cacheSalt scoping, the 30-minute TTL, the per-donation gate, or the DBK3 AAD. The docs do not claim weaker controls. The documented mechanism could mean more frequent donations for dense Qwen, with a slightly different at-rest footprint, but that is within T-041's accepted SEC-035 posture and is not evidenced as a regression.

Open question for integration: whether the underlying code change (EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift and the complete-store capture boundary) was reviewed. It is not in this batch. Check that it still passes through the per-donation adoption/benefit gate and the salt-folded HMAC tags, and that the T-041 detection_hint list covers it. Documentation-only here, so no finding.
